issues.description: Class Person: the common model in the solution repository declares the first-name property as 'givenName' with accessors getGivenName()/setGivenName() (src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java in the solution). The template repository, the problem statement UML and the rest of the code (clients and services) expect the property to be named 'firstName' with getFirstName()/setFirstName() (e.g. template common Person, client PersonScene and server PersonService). This naming mismatch will cause compilation failures (missing methods) and prevents students from running or comparing solution code with the template and the described API/UI behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person property name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution repository's common Person class to use the field name 'firstName' and provide getFirstName()/setFirstName() (replace 'givenName' and its accessors). Alternatively, update all usages in controllers, views and services to use 'givenName' and its accessors consistently. Ensure the problem statement, template and solution use the same identifier so code compiles and the UI/service behavior matches the specification.
